subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw doctor --fix 4-5x slower on 2026.5.20 vs 2026.5.19 (55s → 229s+) — session snapshot path traversal bottleneck

question: Is the merged stale-session snapshot repair plus v2026.6.11 behavior enough to close this issue, or should maintainers continue through the open repair-sequencing path?
rationale: Source and release evidence prove one subset is fixed, but the central user-visible performance regression has not been live-proven resolved and the remaining candidate PR has correctness/proof blockers.

options.title: Keep Open For Proven Narrow Fix
options.body: Keep this issue open, require redacted current-release/current-main timing proof, and only land a dependency-safe optimization that preserves OAuth repair ordering.

options.title: Sponsor The Existing PR
options.body: A maintainer can take over https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/85670, repair the ordering issue, and ask for or provide live patched-run timing proof before merge.

options.title: Close With Release Proof
options.body: Close this issue only if maintainers can show v2026.6.11 or current main already fixes the 90-session update/doctor timing path in a comparable environment.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For Proven Narrow Fix
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, require redacted current-release/current-main timing proof, and only land a dependency-safe optimization that preserves OAuth repair ordering.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the partial snapshot repair and is the clearest routed owner for deciding whether that proof is enough or whether the blocked optimization path should continue.
